trap-negation-contrast.notes: pass on all ten. TWO FINDINGS, neither fixed inline. (1) 'Each nucleon is a spin-1/2 fermion. It is a single-component knot.' — the second sentence is FALSE in this framework's own terms, and the proof block repeats it more explicitly. The corpus builds each nucleon on the Borromean braid B_3 = (sigma_0 sigma_1^{-1})^3 (rem:meson-to-proton-via-borromean); I computed its closure's permutation, which is the identity on 3 strands, so the closure has THREE components — that is what makes it the Borromean rings. The rest of the corpus agrees: rem:linking-relations-table-table1-data gives p (+) n = 6 components, i.e. 3 per nucleon. Full analysis and why it matters recorded on prf:nuclear-spin-parity. (2) LEAN REF RESOLVES TO A FILE THAT DOES NOT DECLARE IT. lean.ref is qou:QOU.Archimedean.nuclear_spin_parity. Under AGENTS.md 0a resolution the sibling <rootName>.lean is checked FIRST, and predicted-spectra/nuclear-spin-parity.lean exists — but it declares SpinParity, nuclearSpinParity, nuclear_spin_parity_even, nuclear_spin_parity_odd and beta_decay_preserves_spin_parity, and NO declaration named nuclear_spin_parity. The declaration of that exact name lives in the library file lean/QOU/Archimedean/nuclear_spin_parity.lean, which the sibling shadows. Both files also open the same namespace QOU.Archimedean. Proposed: point the ref at one of the sibling's actual names, or remove the sibling so candidate 2 resolves. Two observations on the Lean itself: the sibling's nuclearSpinParity is DEFINED as 'if A % 2 = 0 then integer else halfInteger', so nuclear_spin_parity_even/_odd are unfoldings of that definition rather than derivations of the physics; and the library file is a third instance of the AGENTS.md 3b-cond item-5 shape — 'class NucleusLike' carries the conclusion as the field claim_spin_parity and the theorem's whole proof is 'refine n.claim_spin_parity' (the other two in this batch are metallic_character_knot and noble_gas_characterization). Its '-- Ref:' path points at archimedean-universe/, which does not exist.
